original.title: API: GET /links/{code}/stats and redirect counting
original.spec:
Expose stats and wire click counting into the redirect.

**Where**
- `src/shortlink/api/stats.py`: `StatsResponse`, `create_stats_router(get_service) -> APIRouter`
- `src/shortlink/main.py`: wiring
- `tests/api/test_stats_api.py`

**How**
- `GET /links/{code}/stats` → 200 `{code, url, clicks, created_at, last_clicked_at}` (`last_clicked_at` null until the first click)
- LinkNotFoundError → 404 `"link not found"`; LinkStorageError → 503 `"could not read the stats, try again"`
- main: startup runs `create_links_schema` then `create_stats_schema`; per request, one connection feeds `SqliteLinkRepository`, `SqliteClickStore` (as the LinkService recorder, replacing `NoClickRecorder`) and `StatsService`
- a failure to record a click turns the redirect into 503 (existing LinkStorageError mapping); the click is counted only when the redirect is answered
- `api/stats.py` may import `shortlink.application.links` errors; `main.py` is the only links-side file that changes
acceptance: test: new link → stats 200 with clicks 0, last_clicked_at null, created_at equal to POST's
test: 3 × GET /{code} (302) → stats clicks 3 and last_clicked_at set
test: GET of an unknown code (404) and GET /links/{code}/stats do not change clicks
test: two links are counted separately
test: stats of unknown and malformed codes → 404 `{"detail": "link not found"}`
test: store failure (router mounted on a test app with a service over a failing fake store) → 503 with a string detail, never 500
`uv run lint-imports` keeps `links never imports stats`; no file `shortlink/*/links.py` changes in this plan

state.notes:
Revised task 3 only. The links review (task 549) found that a LinkStorageError raised while FastAPI resolves a dependency (get_service calling connect) returned a raw 500, and that path had no test. Task 3 now copies that guarded-dependency pattern and adds a test for it. Other notes for implementers, on the code as it is now:
- LinkService(repository, recorder, clock, new_code) is in application/links.py, with ClickRecorder (Protocol), NoClickRecorder, LinkNotFoundError, LinkStorageError. LinkService.get already rejects malformed codes via is_valid_code before the repository is read, so stats inherits that.
- persistence/db.py connect() already wraps sqlite3 errors into LinkStorageError and sets foreign_keys=ON, WAL and busy_timeout. SqliteLinkRepository in persistence/links.py is the wrapping pattern to copy.

- Skeleton files exist (docstring only): domain/stats.py, application/stats.py, persistence/stats.py, api/stats.py.
- The concurrency test needs a links row before recording (FK). Create it with create_links_schema plus a SqliteLinkRepository.add.

original.title: Links API: POST /links, GET /{code}, wiring
original.spec:
HTTP routes, error handling and the wiring in create_app.

**Where**
- `src/shortlink/links/api/schemas.py`: `CreateLinkRequest`, `LinkResponse`
- `src/shortlink/links/api/dependencies.py`: `get_create_link`, `get_resolve_link`
- `src/shortlink/links/api/routes.py`: `router`
- `src/shortlink/main.py`: `Settings`, `create_app(settings: Settings | None = None)`, exception handlers
- `tests/conftest.py` (client on a tmp_path db), `tests/links/api/test_links_api.py`

**How**
- `POST /links` body `{"url": str}` (extra fields forbidden) -> 201 `{"code", "url", "created_at"}` (ISO-8601 UTC) with header `Location: /{code}`
- `GET /{code}` -> 302 `RedirectResponse(url, status_code=302)` with `Cache-Control: no-store` so browsers do not skip later clicks
- errors: `InvalidUrl` -> 422 `{"detail": "<message>"}`; `LinkNotFound` -> 404 `{"detail": "link not found"}`; `CodeSpaceExhausted` -> 503 `{"detail": "could not allocate a code, retry"}`; `RequestValidationError` -> 422 with a single string `detail` (e.g. `"body.url: Field required"`)
- `Settings`: frozen dataclass with `db_path: Path`, default from env `SHORTLINK_DB_PATH` or `shortlink.db`; `observers: Sequence[RedirectObserver] = ()` extra hook so click-stats can add its observer
- `create_app` builds `Database`, runs `initialise()` and `create_links_schema`, builds the repo and use cases, stores them on `app.state`, includes the links router **last** so `/{code}` never shadows `/docs`, `/openapi.json` or `/links/...`
- dependencies read use cases from `request.app.state`
acceptance: test: POST /links with a valid URL -> 201, body has a 7-char base62 code, the same url, created_at in UTC, and `Location: /{code}`
test: then GET /{code} with `follow_redirects=False` -> 302, `Location` equals the url, `Cache-Control: no-store`
test: POST with `ftp://x`, empty url, a url with `\n`, a 2049-char url -> 422 with a string detail
test: POST with missing body, non-JSON body, `url` as a number, or an extra field -> 422 with a string detail (never a list)
test: GET /abc (malformed) and GET /zzzzzzz (unknown) -> 404 `{"detail": "link not found"}`
test: the same url posted twice gets two different codes
test: 20 concurrent POSTs (ThreadPoolExecutor on the TestClient) all return 201 with distinct codes
test: with a forced generator always returning a taken code, POST -> 503 with a string detail
test: `/openapi.json` and `/docs` still answer 200 with the catch-all route registered
test: a Settings observer receives exactly one call per successful redirect and none for 404

- Persistence: map IntegrityError to CodeTaken only for the primary key (check the message or the constraint); CHECK violations must not become CodeTaken. The domain validates first, so this is defensive.
- Add __init__.py to each new tests/links/... folder, like tests/__init__.py, so mypy and pytest do not clash on duplicate test basenames.
- The 20-concurrent-POST test shares one TestClient across threads. If it is flaky, build one TestClient per thread or use httpx with the app's ASGI transport.

state.notes: Revised task 4 only. The original plan breaks an existing test: tests/test_app.py expects GET /does-not-exist (a single segment, 14 chars) to return 404 {"detail": "Not Found"}. With the catch-all GET /{code}, that path now reaches ResolveLink and returns 404 {"detail": "link not found"}. plan.goal: Clients can POST a http/https URL to /links and get back a random 7-character base62 code; GET /{code} answers 302 to the stored URL, and lets observers (click-stats, next plan) know about each successful redirect.
out_of_scope: auth, custom aliases, expiration, edit/delete, rate limiting, per-click history (whole wave)
counting clicks (click-stats plan); this plan only calls observers
deduplicating identical URLs: every POST creates a new code
blocking internal hosts or private IPs: the service never fetches the URL, so there is no SSRF; any http/https URL with a host is accepted
phishing or malware checks on target URLs
schema migrations framework: the schema is created with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on startup
returning an absolute short URL (needs a configured base URL); the response carries the code

design.why: Two small tables; the stack says SQLite and the user accepted stdlib sqlite3.
design.chosen: repository per aggregate on stdlib sqlite3

options.name: repository per aggregate on stdlib sqlite3
options.tradeoffs: One class owns all SQL of an aggregate, no ORM dependency; hand-written mapping and schema.

options.name: SQLAlchemy Core/ORM
options.tradeoffs: Typed queries and easier migrations later; a heavy dependency and mypy friction for two tables.

design.why: stdlib sqlite3 is sync; a connection per operation keeps it thread-safe.

options.name: sync endpoints and repositories
options.tradeoffs: Plain sqlite3, FastAPI runs them in its threadpool; no async driver.

options.name: async with aiosqlite
options.tradeoffs: Fits FastAPI's async style; extra dependency and no real gain on a local file database.

design.why: User picked it: keeps the feature contract one-directional (stats -> links.application) with the redirect rule in links.
design.topic: how click counting hooks into the redirect

options.name: RedirectObserver port in links.application
options.tradeoffs: links never imports stats and import-linter enforces it; one extra protocol.

options.name: click counter inside links
options.tradeoffs: Fewer pieces; stats becomes only a read endpoint and links owns counting.

options.name: independent features orchestrated by main.py
options.tradeoffs: Strongest isolation; the redirect rule moves into the composition root.

design.why: Simple and safe for a small API; tests use a file under tmp_path.

options.name: new connection per operation
options.tradeoffs: Thread-safe under FastAPI's threadpool, trivial to reason about; small open cost per call.

options.name: one shared connection with check_same_thread=False and a lock
options.tradeoffs: Cheaper per call; a global lock and lifecycle to manage.
